NKJV.1: I am the rose of Sharon, And the lily of the valleys.
NKJV.2: Like a lily among thorns, So is my love among the daughters.
NKJV.3: Like an apple tree among the trees of the woods, So is my beloved among the sons. I sat down in his shade with great delight, And his fruit was sweet to my taste.
NKJV.4: He brought me to the banqueting house, And his banner over me was love.
NKJV.5: Sustain me with cakes of raisins, Refresh me with apples, For I am lovesick.
NKJV.6: His left hand is under my head, And his right hand embraces me.
NKJV.7: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, By the gazelles or by the does of the field, Do not stir up nor awaken love Until it pleases.
NKJV.8: The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes Leaping upon the mountains, Skipping upon the hills.
NKJV.9: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Behold, he stands behind our wall; He is looking through the windows, Gazing through the lattice.
NKJV.10: My beloved spoke, and said to me: “Rise up, my love, my fair one, And come away.
NKJV.11: For lo, the winter is past, The rain is over and gone.
NKJV.12: The flowers appear on the earth; The time of singing has come, And the voice of the turtledove Is heard in our land.
NKJV.13: The fig tree puts forth her green figs, And the vines with the tender grapes Give a good smell. Rise up, my love, my fair one, And come away!
NKJV.14: “O my dove, in the clefts of the rock, In the secret places of the cliff, Let me see your face, Let me hear your voice; For your voice is sweet, And your face is lovely.”
NKJV.15: Catch us the foxes, The little foxes that spoil the vines, For our vines have tender grapes.
NKJV.16: My beloved is mine, and I am his. He feeds his flock among the lilies.
NKJV.17: Until the day breaks And the shadows flee away, Turn, my beloved, And be like a gazelle Or a young stag Upon the mountains of Bether.

ESV.1: I am a rose  of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.
ESV.2: As a lily among brambles, so is my love among the young women.
ESV.3: As an apple tree among the trees of the forest, so is my beloved among the young men. With great delight I sat in his shadow, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.
ESV.4: He brought me to the banqueting house,  and his banner over me was love.
ESV.5: Sustain me with raisins; refresh me with apples, for I am sick with love.
ESV.6: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me!
ESV.7: I adjure you,  O daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or the does of the field, that you not stir up or awaken love until it pleases.
ESV.8: The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes, leaping over the mountains, bounding over the hills.
ESV.9: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Behold, there he stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, looking through the lattice.
ESV.10: My beloved speaks and says to me: “Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away,
ESV.11: for behold, the winter is past; the rain is over and gone.
ESV.12: The flowers appear on the earth, the time of singing  has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.
ESV.13: The fig tree ripens its figs, and the vines are in blossom; they give forth fragrance. Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.
ESV.14: O my dove, in the clefts of the rock, in the crannies of the cliff, let me see your face, let me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet, and your face is lovely.
ESV.15: Catch the foxes  for us, the little foxes that spoil the vineyards, for our vineyards are in blossom.”
ESV.16: My beloved is mine, and I am his; he grazes  among the lilies.
ESV.17: Until the day breathes and the shadows flee, turn, my beloved, be like a gazelle or a young stag on cleft mountains.

AMP.1:
"I am the rose [of the plain] of Sharon,
The lily of the valleys [that grows in deep places]."
AMP.2:
(The Bridegroom) "Like the lily among the thorns,
So are you, my darling, among the maidens."
AMP.3:
(The Shulammite Bride) "Like an apple tree [rare and welcome] among the trees of the forest,
So is my beloved among the young men!
In his shade I took great delight and sat down,
And his fruit was sweet and delicious to my palate.
AMP.4:
"He has brought me to his banqueting place,
And his banner over me is love [waving overhead to protect and comfort me].
AMP.5:
"Sustain me with raisin cakes,
Refresh me with apples,
Because I am sick with love.
AMP.6:
"Let his left hand be under my head
And his right hand embrace me."
AMP.7:
(The Bridegroom) "I command that you take an oath, O daughters of Jerusalem,
By the gazelles or by the does of the field [which run free],
That you do not rouse nor awaken my love
Until she pleases."
AMP.8:
(The Shulammite Bride) "Listen! My beloved!
Behold, he comes,
Climbing on the mountains,
Leaping and running on the hills!
AMP.9:
"My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag.
Behold, he is standing behind our wall,
He is looking through the windows,
He is gazing through the lattice.
AMP.10:
"My beloved speaks and says to me,
'Arise, my love, my fair one,
And come away.
AMP.11:
'For behold, the winter is past,
The rain is over and gone.
AMP.12:
'The flowers appear on the earth once again;
The time for singing has come,
And the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.
AMP.13:
'The fig tree has budded and ripens her figs,
And the vines are in blossom and give forth their fragrance.
Arise, my love, my fair one,
And come away [to climb the rocky steps of the hillside].'"
AMP.14:
(The Bridegroom) "O my dove, [here] in the clefts in the rock,
In the sheltered and secret place of the steep pathway,
Let me see your face,
Let me hear your voice;
For your voice is sweet,
And your face is lovely."
AMP.15:
(The Chorus) "Catch the foxes for us,
The little foxes that spoil and ruin the vineyards [of love],
While our vineyards are in blossom."
AMP.16:
(The Shulammite Bride) "My beloved is mine and I am his;
He pastures his flock among the lilies.
AMP.17:
"Until the cool of the day when the shadows flee away,
Return quickly, my beloved, and be like a gazelle
Or a young stag on the mountains of Bether [which separate us]."

NLT.1:
I am the spring crocus blooming on the Sharon Plain,
the lily of the valley.
NLT.2:
Like a lily among thistles
is my darling among young women.
NLT.3:
Like the finest apple tree in the orchard
is my lover among other young men.
I sit in his delightful shade
and taste his delicious fruit.
NLT.4:
He escorts me to the banquet hall;
it’s obvious how much he loves me.
NLT.5:
Strengthen me with raisin cakes,
refresh me with apples,
for I am weak with love.
NLT.6:
His left arm is under my head,
and his right arm embraces me.
NLT.7:
Promise me, O women of Jerusalem,
by the gazelles and wild deer,
not to awaken love until the time is right.
NLT.8:
Ah, I hear my lover coming!
He is leaping over the mountains,
bounding over the hills.
NLT.9:
My lover is like a swift gazelle
or a young stag.
Look, there he is behind the wall,
looking through the window,
peering into the room.
NLT.10:
My lover said to me,
“Rise up, my darling!
Come away with me, my fair one!
NLT.11:
Look, the winter is past,
and the rains are over and gone.
NLT.12:
The flowers are springing up,
the season of singing birds has come,
and the cooing of turtledoves fills the air.
NLT.13:
The fig trees are forming young fruit,
and the fragrant grapevines are blossoming.
Rise up, my darling!
Come away with me, my fair one!”
NLT.14:
My dove is hiding behind the rocks,
behind an outcrop on the cliff.
Let me see your face;
let me hear your voice.
For your voice is pleasant,
and your face is lovely.
NLT.15:
Catch all the foxes,
those little foxes,
before they ruin the vineyard of love,
for the grapevines are blossoming!
NLT.16:
My lover is mine, and I am his.
He browses among the lilies.
NLT.17:
Before the dawn breezes blow
and the night shadows flee,
return to me, my love, like a gazelle
or a young stag on the rugged mountains.

MSG.1:
I'm just a wildflower picked from the plains of Sharon,
a lotus blossom from the valley pools.
MSG.2:
A lotus blossoming in a swamp of weeds—
that's my dear friend among the girls in the village.
MSG.3:
As an apricot tree stands out in the forest,
my lover stands above the young men in town.
All I want is to sit in his shade,
to taste and savor his delicious love.
MSG.4:
He took me home with him for a festive meal,
but his eyes feasted on me!
MSG.5:
Oh! Give me something refreshing to eat—and quickly!
Apricots, raisins—anything. I'm about to faint with love!
MSG.6:
His left hand cradles my head,
and his right arm encircles my waist!
MSG.7:
Oh, let me warn you, sisters in Jerusalem,
by the gazelles, yes, by all the wild deer:
Don't excite love, don't stir it up,
until the time is ripe—and you're ready.
MSG.8:
Look! Listen! There's my lover!
Do you see him coming?
Vaulting the mountains,
leaping the hills.
MSG.9:
My lover is like a gazelle, graceful;
like a young stag, virile.
Look at him there, on tiptoe at the gate,
all ears, all eyes—ready!
MSG.10:
My lover has arrived
and he's speaking to me!
Get up, my dear friend,
fair and beautiful lover—come to me!
MSG.11:
Look around you: Winter is over;
the winter rains are over, gone!
MSG.12:
Spring flowers are in blossom all over.
The whole world's a choir—and singing!
Spring warblers are filling the forest
with sweet arpeggios.
MSG.13:
Lilacs are exuberantly purple and perfumed,
and cherry trees fragrant with blossoms.
Oh, get up, dear friend,
my fair and beautiful lover—come to me!
MSG.14:
Come, my shy and modest dove—
leave your seclusion, come out in the open.
Let me see your face,
let me hear your voice.
For your voice is soothing
and your face is ravishing.
MSG.15:
Then you must protect me from the foxes,
foxes on the prowl,
Foxes who would like nothing better
than to get into our flowering garden.
MSG.16:
My lover is mine, and I am his.
Nightly he strolls in our garden,
Delighting in the flowers
MSG.17:
until dawn breathes its light and night slips away.
Turn to me, dear lover.
Come like a gazelle.
Leap like a wild stag
on delectable mountains!

in the covert of the cliff,
let me see your face,
let me hear your voice;
for your voice is sweet,
and your face is lovely.
NRSVCE.15:
Catch us the foxes,
the little foxes,
that ruin the vineyards —
for our vineyards are in blossom.”
NRSVCE.16:
My beloved is mine and I am his;
he pastures his flock among the lilies.
NRSVCE.17:
Until the day breathes
and the shadows flee,
turn, my beloved, be like a gazelle
or a young stag on the cleft mountains.

NET.1: I am a meadow flower from Sharon, a lily from the valleys.
NET.2: Like a lily among the thorns, so is my darling among the maidens.
NET.3: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, so is my beloved among the young men. I delight to sit in his shade, and his fruit is sweet to my taste.
NET.4: He brought me into the banquet hall, and he looked at me lovingly.
NET.5: Sustain me with raisin cakes, refresh me with apples, for I am faint with love. The Double Refrain: Embracing and Adjuration
NET.6: His left hand caresses my head, and his right hand stimulates me.
NET.7: I adjure you, O maidens of Jerusalem, by the gazelles and by the young does of the open fields: Do not awaken or arouse love until it pleases!
NET.8: Listen! My lover is approaching! Look! Here he comes, leaping over the mountains, bounding over the hills!
NET.9: My lover is like a gazelle or a young stag. Look! There he stands behind our wall, gazing through the window, peering through the lattice.
NET.10: My lover spoke to me, saying: “Arise, my darling; My beautiful one, come away with me!
NET.11: Look! The winter has passed, the winter rains are over and gone.
NET.12: The pomegranates have appeared in the land, the time for pruning and singing has come; the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.
NET.13: The fig tree has budded, the vines have blossomed and give off their fragrance. Arise, come away my darling; my beautiful one, come away with me!”
NET.14: O my dove, in the clefts of the rock, in the hiding places of the mountain crags, let me see your face, let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your face is lovely.
NET.15: Catch the foxes for us, the little foxes, that ruin the vineyards — for our vineyard is in bloom.
NET.16: My lover is mine and I am his; he grazes among the lilies.
NET.17: Until the dawn arrives and the shadows flee, turn, my beloved — be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountain gorges.
